body.hook: The job you'll have in 15 years might not exist yet. But the skills you build now, in kitchens, shops, studios and labs, connect to whole families of careers. Alberta organizes them into five CTS clusters.

study.title: Map My Path
study.question: How can CTS courses connect my interests to careers?
study.passage:
The five CTS clusters in Alberta:
• Business, Administration, Finance and Information Technology (BIT): computing science, financial management, enterprise and innovation, information processing, networking
• Health, Recreation and Human Services (HRH): foods, cosmetology, health care, human and social services, recreation leadership, child development
• Media, Design and Communication Arts (MDC): communication technology, design studies, fashion studies
• Natural Resources (NAT): agriculture, environmental stewardship, forestry, primary resources, wildlife
• Trades, Manufacturing and Transportation (TMT): construction technologies, electro-technologies, fabrication, mechanics, logistics
Courses are 1 credit each at introductory (1000), intermediate (2000) and advanced (3000) levels; some have prerequisites.
Part 1, Interest inventory (10 minutes): Rate 20 activities (fixing things, helping people, designing, working outdoors, organizing data).
Part 2, Cluster match (10 minutes): Find your top two clusters.
Part 3, Occupation research (20 minutes): Use alis.alberta.ca (Alberta Learning Information Service) to research two occupations: duties, education needed, wages, outlook.
Part 4, Pathway (10 minutes): Map CTS courses from introductory to advanced that lead toward one occupation.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson; cluster information summarized from Alberta Education CTS program materials and alis.alberta.ca.
